Found where the author gets set. I'm sending the fix to codex-10 now, with a park on the job.㊥ Gist: codex-10 is now fixing the author problem, so that a park wake-up or other harness turn is no longer recorded under your name. Only turns you typed will keep author "joe". Old records stay as they are, and I'll review the change when codex-10 reports back.

㊯ (the job) You can poll it yourself:
- job: `invoke-1790887039716-29818-9dffc29a` (running on codex-10)
- my park: `park-cbb7534e-bb06-4cff-bb00-8753535f615c`, with a 45-minute deadline

The fault is in `agent-chat.el`, in `agent-chat-emit-turn-evidence!`. That function sets the author to your login name for every user-role turn. It does this even though the same record's origin field already says the turn came from the harness, as a park resume. The fix:
- **Author rule:** sets the author from that origin.
- **Session-start records:** applies the same rule there; they have the same fault.
- **Test:** must fail if the old author line is put back.

Before changing anything, codex-10 has to check every reader that looks up your turns by `author=joe`, such as the harvest scripts, the turn stepper and the turnfeed, and report whether each still works.

㊢ (backfill) The backfill is running. Coverage is now 4,856 of 4,927 (98.6%); the total went up by two because you've typed two new turns since. Each pack of ten takes 3–14 minutes, so the first lines in the loop log should show up shortly.

(what's queued) The 68 pending turns, in the order the loop takes them:
1. **Minard window (22 Aug–21 Sep):** 2 turns.
2. **26–27 September:** 8 of your turns that were never read. The batch harvest ended at 26 September 03:14, and origin stamping only began on 27 September, so these fell between the two.
3. **Live retries:** 55 live readings that were stuck at "requested" or had failed. I copied them into a retry batch and left the live originals untouched. When the retry reads one, the coverage count treats it as read.

(watching progress)
- `python3 ~/code/futon3c/scripts/xiang_coverage.py` prints read, refused and pending per window, then the total. `--line` gives just the total line. It takes 0.15 s, so `watch` is cheap. Committed as futon3c `f70a2ed1`.
- `tail -f ~/code/storage/operator-turns/backfill-loop.jsonl` shows one line per finished pack: seat, turns, published, refused, and the reasons.
- To stop it: `touch /tmp/claude17/backfill-loop.STOP`.

previous_reply_acts.text: (pipes, your point from last turn) You were right that automated traffic was getting in among your turns, and it was worse than I'd said. Before origin stamping began on 27 September, park wake-ups were delivered with "From: joe / Origin: operator" headers. Of the 339 turns from that gap that looked like yours, 330 were park wake-ups and 8 were inbox-zero notices. I filtered them out with the existing `xiang2000_p6o3` classifier before queueing. The live readings were not affected: only 1 of about 1,140 is a park wake-up. Since the 27th, wake-ups are labelled as harness traffic, but they are still filed in futon1b with **author "joe"**. That is 652 of them since then, so any query by author still mixes them in with your turns.
